newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Underground Thorncliffe chrome mine opens.
newsitem.headline: Underground Thorncliffe chrome mine opens.

text.p: South Africa's Consolidated Metallurgical Industries Ltd (CMI) on Thursday officially opened its new Thorncliffe underground chrome mine, which is set to become one of the largest in the world when it is fully operational.
Thorncliffe will have an initial underground annual capacity rate of 500,000 tonnes of chrome ore.
"However, due to strength of demand, it is likely the capacity of the underground mine will have to be increased to one million tonnes per annum," controlling shareholder JCI Ltd said in a statement.
The mine, near Lydenburg about 300 km east of Johannesburg, was opened by Mpumalanga Province premier Matthews Phosa.
"Thorncliffe mine will enhance CMI's position as a low-cost ferrochrome producer for many years to come," JCI said.

Direct investment in capital equipment for underground mining, the surface infrastructure and beneficiation plants is not expected to exceed 70 million rand for the one million tonne capacity, JCI said.

CMI acquired Thorncliffe from JCI in March 1996. This gave it access to about 27 million tonnes of proven chrome ore reserves in situ. Acquiring Thorncliffe, CMI began opencast mining operations to a depth of 32 metres, which is conducted at an annual rate of 500,000 tonnes run-of-mine.
"Sufficient reserves are available to sustain this operation for another four years," JCI said.
The underground mine's production is currently approaching a 250,000 tonne annual rate. Initial mining depth is planned to be restricted to 300 metres.
At full production Thorncliffe is expected to provide 350 jobs.
